memory_versions.text:
Working notes: Order intake

- Order form v1 required fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Each intake batch allows 3 attempts. Rejection costs -0.20. After 3 rejections, record goes to manual review; move to next batch.
- Observed ORD-5100–5109: all rejected.
- cust, email, order_date were never marked invalid.
- priority was invalid in 10/10 rejections. Always verify priority.
- qty was invalid in 3/10 (early batches).
- ship_country was invalid in 8/10.
- Invalid fields often correspond to fields missing/truncated in the source excerpt, especially priority, qty, ship_country.
- Source type and front-desk wording varied (handwritten transcription, phone confirmation, emailed order, partner portal) but did not predict success.
- Do not guess missing priority, qty, or ship_country. Attempts are scarce.
- Before submitting, confirm all six required fields are present and valid. If source data is incomplete, preserve attempts and seek clarification/manual review rather than resubmitting likely-invalid forms.
- Seen customers: Cy Reyes, Bo Okafor, Dee Reyes, Eli Okafor. Seen emails: user778, user881, user177, user506 @example.com. These specifics are probably not useful beyond batch history.

Working notes: Order intake

- Form v1 required: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Attempts are limited to 3 per order/record across successive intake batches. Rejection costs -0.20. After 3 failures, record goes to manual review; move to next record.
- ORD-5110–5119 confirm priority is the most persistent invalid field. ship_country is also often invalid. qty is occasionally invalid. cust/email/order_date are usually valid, but can be invalid if the source or submitted JSON is garbled/truncated (ORD-5119).
- Invalid fields often correspond to missing/truncated source excerpt or submitted JSON, especially priority, qty, ship_country. Do not guess missing fields. Confirm all six fields are present and valid before using an attempt.
- Source type and front-desk wording (emailed order, voicemail, partner portal, duplicate-check message, priority marking) do not reliably predict success. “Marked ordinary priority” did not make priority valid in several cases.
- A third attempt can succeed when enough valid data is available (ORD-5114), but repeated submission of incomplete/truncated source data still fails.
- If source data is incomplete after prior rejections, preserve remaining attempts and seek clarification/manual review instead of resubmitting likely-invalid forms.
- Customer/batch specifics are mostly useful as history only; they are not predictive.

Working notes: Order intake

- Form v1/v2 require: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Fields are the same for both versions.
- Max 3 attempts per order/record across batches. Rejection costs -0.20. After 3 failures, record goes to manual review; move to next record.
- ORD-5110–5129 confirm priority is the most persistent invalid field, often alone or with ship_country. ship_country is often invalid. qty is sometimes invalid. cust/email/order_date are usually valid unless source/submitted JSON is missing, truncated, or garbled (ORD-5119; ORD-5127 empty submission).
- Invalid fields usually correspond to missing/truncated source excerpt or submitted JSON. Do not guess missing fields. Confirm all six fields are present and valid before using an attempt.
- Source type and front-desk wording are not predictive: emailed order, voicemail, partner portal, handwritten transcription, duplicate-check message, and “ordinary priority” all still failed. “Marked ordinary priority” does not make priority valid.
- Attempt 3 can succeed only with enough valid data. Repeated submission of incomplete/truncated source still fails (ORD-5120, 5123, 5126, 5129). If source remains incomplete after prior rejections, preserve remaining attempts and seek clarification/manual review instead of resubmitting likely-invalid forms.
- Customer/batch specifics are mostly useful as history only; they are not predictive.

Working notes: Order intake

- Forms v1/v2 need: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Same fields for both versions.
- Max 3 attempts per order/record. Rejection costs -0.20. After 3 failures, manual review; move to next record.
- ORD-5110–5139 confirm priority is the most persistent invalid field, often alone or with ship_country. ship_country is often invalid. qty is sometimes invalid. cust/email/order_date are usually valid when present.
- Invalid fields usually match missing/truncated/garbled source or submitted JSON. Do not guess missing fields. Confirm all six fields are present and valid before using an attempt.
- Source type and front-desk wording are not predictive: emailed order, voicemail, partner portal, handwritten transcription, duplicate-check message, call-to-confirm, and “ordinary priority” all still failed. “Marked ordinary priority” does not make priority valid.
- Attempt 3 can succeed only with enough valid data. Resubmitting incomplete/truncated source keeps failing (ORD-5120, 5123, 5126, 5129, 5130–5139). If source remains incomplete after rejection, preserve remaining attempts and seek clarification/manual review instead of resubmitting likely-invalid forms.
- Repeated same customer/source across attempts does not guarantee validity; truncation can still invalidate priority, ship_country, or qty.
- Customer/batch specifics are history only; not predictive.
